summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM and agent-based applications grow more complex and expensive, with the market expanding at a 30%+ CAGR yet only about 15% of GenAI deployments currently instrumenting any observability (projected to hit 50% by 2028 per Gartner). Observability tools track traces, costs, latency, and output quality—helping teams catch failures that break differently in agentic systems while controlling unpredictable API spend. 2026 is a consolidation year, marked by ClickHouse acquiring Langfuse and Braintrust raising an $80M Series B.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end LLM application tracing, token usage, latency, cost, evaluation metrics, and production monitoring—especially tightly integrated with the LangChain ecosystem.
features: Detailed trace visualization and debugging of chains/agents
tools.pricing: Usage-priced; roughly $264 per 100,000 traces per analyses in 2026. Trace costs can run ~5–10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads. Free developer tier available.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain/LangGraph who want deep, framework-native tracing and evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, cost per department/user/model, token usage, latency, and request/response logging via a lightweight proxy.
features: Single-line base URL change for integration (setup in under 5 minutes)
tools.pricing: Generous free tier; usage-priced. Helicone Pro reaches 100,000 traces at ~$79 per Markaicode—a fraction of comparable LangSmith pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting fast, low-overhead cost visibility and governance across any LLM provider without framework lock-in.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: Combined ML and LLM workloads—experiment tracking, model performance, LLM traces, evaluations, and unified monitoring across both traditional ML and GenAI.
features: Unified ML + LLM observability via W&B Weave
LLM trace logging and evaluation workflows
Integration with broader W&B MLOps platform
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans are subscription/usage-based with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams running both ML and LLM workloads who want a single platform for unified model and GenAI monitoring.

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize AX / Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM and ML observability—traces, embeddings, drift, data quality, evaluation metrics, and enterprise production monitoring.
features: Phoenix open-source entry point for traces, experiments, and evaluators
Arize AX hosted dashboards with data retention
Embedding and drift analysis rooted in ML observability
tools.pricing: Phoenix (OSS) is free to self-host; Arize AX offered via hosted cloud and enterprise contracts (custom pricing).
tools.best_for: ML-mature teams wanting to bring established ML observability practices into LLM tracing, with an open-source-to-enterprise upgrade path.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token/cost tracking, latency, prompt management, evaluations, and production analytics—framework-agnostic and open source.
features: Detailed tracing and nested span visualization
Cost and token analytics per model
tools.pricing: Self-host is free (compute + storage costs only), often the cheapest option; managed cloud is usage-priced with a free tier. Acquired by ClickHouse in January 2026.
tools.best_for: Cost-conscious teams wanting a flexible, open-source observability stack they can self-host and fully control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM and agent telemetry via OpenTelemetry-compliant spans—traces, token usage, latency, and errors across any stack.
features: Near-zero integration overhead (e.g., single-line OpenAIInstrumentor().instrument() in Python)
Works across any backend that accepts OTel data
Ideal for multi-framework and polyglot setups
tools.pricing: Open source and free; costs come only from the chosen OpenTelemetry backend/destination.
tools.best_for: Multi-framework or standards-first teams wanting vendor-neutral, drop-in instrumentation that exports to any observability backend.

cost_tips: Use response caching (e.g., via Helicone proxy) to avoid paying for repeated or near-identical requests, which can dramatically cut spend on high-traffic endpoints.
Right-size your models—route simple tasks to smaller/cheaper models and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning, using cheaper models for classification, routing, and summarization.
Instrument per-user and per-department cost tracking to catch runaway spend early; observability trace costs can reach 5–10% of LLM API spend, so sample or self-host (e.g., Langfuse) at high volume.
Reduce token usage by trimming prompts, compressing context/RAG retrievals, setting sensible max-token limits, and batching requests where latency allows.
